narr: A band of thunderstorms containing rainfall rates up to two inches per hour trained over parts of northwest Kentucky. The storms produced some urban flash flooding. The storms intensified during the heat of the day ahead of a 500 mb shortwave trough drifting eastward toward the Ohio River Valley. A tropical air mass was firmly entrenched, with precipitable water values well above the 90th percentile for early September. Effective vertical wind shear from 20 to 25 knots resulted in loosely organized bands of storms. The mean steering flow was parallel to the synoptic forcing, which caused training of the bands of storms with heavy rainfall.
ev: Flash flooding was reported along Highway 41 in the retail area on the east side of Henderson.

A number of roadways were flooded in and around Owensboro, including Carter Road. Storm total rainfall ranged up to 5.48 inches at a rain gage on the west side of Owensboro, near the east end of the Audubon Parkway where it meets Highway 60. A residential neighborhood in the immediate vicinity of this gage was flooded. There was also a report of 5.37 inches a mile west of the Owensboro airport.
